title: How his band compared with other bands
summary: He says his band was a good simple dance and theatrical band, not as musically varied as Ellington's.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: How would you compare your band to some of the other very popular bands at that time in terms of what you were doing musically?

Well, we had a good dance band. We weren't, I wasn't no Duke Ellington. You know, for musical variety, because we didn't have those type arrangements. We had a good, simple arrangement where people could hum and they could feel the rhythm and dance to it.

So, we used to draw very big on account of that. But, the bands, we had a good theatrical band. We could present ourselves. We did a little clowning while other bands just sat there and played straight. And, the people went for us very much.
And, I got the tempo and these people would just sit up there in front of us. And, there's usually 5,000 people in front of you. And, the floor was going up and down like this.
So, when I found that that's what they liked to do, I stayed with it. So, they used to love that.

But, compared with the other bands, they were straight for what they had to do, you know, musically speaking. But, I did add a lot of little different things with a little of this and a little of that, you know, just to get around people, like a concert, like they like. And so I stuck with it and I had a little fun.
